nodes.content:
"""Rasterize Buildings: SCOUT's building rasterizer, "OSM vector to raster".

Input: a buildings layer, a GeoDataFrame of polygons with a CRS and a column
of heights in metres.
Output: one raster in EPSG:3395, each cell a height in metres: the 256 by 256
map tiles SCOUT draws, 8-bit gray where 255 is the maximum height, side by
side. A tile SCOUT writes no file for, because no building is near it, is no
data. An Autark map draws it as input_0, band band_1, and SCOUT's Deep Umbra
shadow model (Accumulated Shadow) reads it.
The Widgets tab sets the height column, the zoom level and the maximum height.
Ported from SCOUT, https://github.com/urban-toolkit/scout.
"""
from scout_rasters.node_outputs import rasterize_buildings

return rasterize_buildings(
    input_0,
    attribute=[!! attribute !!],
    zoom=int([!! zoom !!]),
    max_height=float([!! max_height !!]),
    output_file=curio_output_file,
)
nodes.goal: Rasterize the existing buildings into one zoom-16 height raster.
Predict the existing buildings' accumulated shadow with Deep Umbra.

nodes.content:
# Statistics: the mean, median, minimum, maximum and count of a
# raster's cells, nodata left out, as a table of one row.
# input_0 is the accumulated shadow in minutes, input_1 the heights it was
# predicted from, as the mask: SCOUT's metrics count the ground, the cells
# Deep Umbra reads as gray level 0, a height under 1.08 m.
from scout_rasters.raster_algebra import raster_statistics

return raster_statistics(input_0, mask=input_1, where=lambda height: height < 1.08)
nodes.goal: Take the mean and median accumulated shadow over the existing buildings' ground.
nodes.title: Shadow over the ground

nodes.content:
# Edit Features writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [
    {"op": "remove", "ids": [8, 10, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19, 31, 34, 51, 66, 77, 82, 106, 122], "label": "SCOUT's 15 removed buildings"},
], key="building_id")

# Towers removed's accumulated shadow, on input_1, minus Existing's, on
# input_0, cell by cell, in minutes: below zero where removing the towers
# takes shadow away, 0 where nothing changes.
from scout_rasters.raster_algebra import raster_calculate

return raster_calculate("subtract", [input_1, input_0], output_file=curio_output_file)
